Fixes dotnet/runtime#135094.

## Summary

Skip the early TLS connection-info query during certificate validation on
**Android 8.1 / API 27 only**. Keep certificate validation and its callback in
place, and populate the real negotiated connection information after the
handshake completes.


## Root cause

The certificate-validation callback runs before the TLS 1.2 handshake has
installed its write-cipher context. On Android 8.1, Conscrypt's
`NativeCrypto_SSL_get_current_cipher` passes the result of
`SSL_get_current_cipher()` directly to `SSL_CIPHER_standard_name()` without a null
check.

A native debugger and a retained full core both identify the fault:

```text
SSL_CIPHER_standard_name
  <- NativeCrypto_SSL_get_current_cipher
  <- AndroidCryptoNative_SSLStreamGetCipherSuite

rdi = 0
faulting instruction: mov 0x8(%rdi),%rax
```

The managed SSL handle and Java session are valid. The null pointer is the
current cipher returned inside Android, so checking the returned managed string
or catching a managed exception cannot prevent this crash.

The early connection-info query exists to support callbacks that inspect
`SslProtocol` or cipher properties. The workaround deliberately preserves that
behavior outside API 27. Earlier Android implementations use a different,
null-safe session-cipher accessor; Android 9 / API 28 adds the missing null check.

Relevant platform sources:
- [Android 8.1 Conscrypt cipher query](https://android.googlesource.com/platform/external/conscrypt/+/android-8.1.0_r1/common/src/jni/main/cpp/NativeCrypto.cpp)
- [Android 8.1 BoringSSL current-cipher lookup](https://android.googlesource.com/platform/external/boringssl/+/android-8.1.0_r1/src/ssl/ssl_lib.cc)
- [Android 9 Conscrypt null check](https://android.googlesource.com/platform/external/conscrypt/+/android-9.0.0_r1/common/src/jni/main/cpp/conscrypt/native_crypto.cc)

## Behavior and regression coverage

On API 27, negotiated-property getters remain unavailable during the inline
validation callback and throw the existing `InvalidOperationException` rather
than causing a native process crash. After authentication, the normal
handshake-success path provides the actual negotiated protocol and cipher.
Certificate, chain, hostname and policy validation are not bypassed.

Strengthen the existing `SslStream_CustomRootTrust_NoChainErrors` test to verify:
- the callback receives the expected sender, certificate and chain;
- acceptance still requires no certificate policy errors;
- API 27 defers negotiated-property availability, while newer Android retains
  early protocol availability;
- the callback runs exactly once and both endpoints authenticate;
- the final cipher is defined, nonzero and matches on both endpoints.

## Validation

Built and tested on public `main` at
`4f53c31f31a6c563aa482fd3d6308f4a575c178e`, using CoreCLR Android x64.

| Run | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Regression test before the product fix, API 27 | Reproduces SIGSEGV at `0x8`; XHarness exit **80 / APP_CRASH** |
| Same regression before the fix, API 29 | **1 passed**, no failures or skips |
| AndroidPlatformTrust suite after the fix, API 27 | **18 passed**, no failures or skips |
| AndroidPlatformTrust suite after the fix, API 29 | **18 passed**, no failures or skips |

Successful build commands:

```sh
./build.sh clr+libs -os android -arch x64 -rc Release -lc Release
./build.sh tasks -os android -arch x64 -c Release
./build.sh libs.sfx+libs.pretest -os android -arch x64 -rc Release -lc Release /p:RuntimeFlavor=CoreCLR
./dotnet.sh build src/libraries/System.Net.Security/tests/AndroidPlatformTrustTests/System.Net.Security.AndroidPlatformTrust.Tests.csproj -c Release /p:TargetOS=android /p:TargetArchitecture=x64 /p:RuntimeFlavor=CoreCLR
```

All four commands completed with exit 0. The regression was built with the test
changes but without the product guard to establish the failing case.

The test APKs ran through XHarness in non-privileged, KVM-accelerated API 27 and
API 29 containers. The after-fix runs exclude `OuterLoop` external-network cases.
API 24/26/28 scope reasoning is from platform source inspection, not emulator
execution. ARM64, Mono, NativeAOT and desktop execution were not tested.
